analysis: The only change in this PR is a test-only addition in ProviderModelSwitchTests.swift (head lines 683-687). It asserts, in failedCommitPreservesMatchingHashAndFingerprint, that after a failed or unconfirmed model-switch commit `autopilotBusyReasons()` does not contain `.modelSwitch`. It also asserts that `.draining` is present only when the connection was dropped, meaning the commit is unconfirmed and admission stays closed (`state.refusingNewWork == dropConnection`). No production code, trust boundary, key handling, attestation, wire protocol or cache storage logic changes. The assertions reinforce fail-closed behavior: an unconfirmed coordinator commit keeps admission closed, and a switch failure releases the switch task. I also checked the surrounding test file for risky patterns. It uses temporary directories and a mock coordinator with no secrets. It exercises rollback of config presence, weight-hash and fingerprint preservation, and the coordinator drain barrier. None of these introduce new attack surface. The threat entries T-012, T-027 and TB-002 are touched only indirectly through test coverage. The production semantics of `autopilotBusyReasons` live outside the supplied evidence, so the correctness of the `.draining` and `.modelSwitch` contract is unverified here. That is a test-fidelity question rather than a security regression. No threat-model update is needed.
